component.name: kmixdeck
component.summary: A streamer's audio mixer for KDE Plasma on PipeWire

description.p: Route every application into its own channel, build as many output mixes as you need (what you hear vs. what the stream hears), and set each channel's level independently per mix.

Playback into a channel: the daemon plays a file or a streamed body into any channel, from the CLI, the window, the web UI or an HTTP play endpoint that starts playing while the body still arrives. An opt-in capture source per channel gives OBS one clean stem per channel.

Cells are gains of one filter chain per channel on a shared bus, so large desks cost a fraction of the nodes they did. The layout file is re-read while running, and two writers no longer overwrite each other. An absent input device no longer stalls every capture source.

Global shortcuts through the GlobalShortcuts portal, the tray popover as a layer-shell surface on Wayland, and a soundboard that plays in the daemon. EBU R128 loudness shows in all four frontends, is published without a meter subscriber, and stays bounded in memory however long the daemon runs.

Meters and loudness analysers are built only against nodes that exist, so a mix created under load is measured instead of silently unlinked; an edge that arrives late clears the error it caused, and its retry no longer leaves a second copy behind. Levels.Peaks is a{sd} on the wire, as documented.

Named scenes: store a full mix state and recall it from any frontend. EBU R128 loudness measurement per mix, and a broadcast limiter that lands on the summed signal instead of the individual channels.

Large desks work: a 32x32 interface no longer loses routing edges at the file-descriptor limit, virtual devices patch through, and rewiring retargets the existing links instead of rebuilding them. Port labels follow the device's own numbering, whether it counts from zero or one.
New BUILD_KDE_FRONTEND option so headless hosts build the service, CLI and web bridge without pulling in the desktop stack. Warnings (-Wall -Wextra) are on by default.
Unit and integration test grid, logging categories, and D-Bus documentation at 100% coverage.

First release. Channels × mixes with independent per-mix levels on PipeWire; per-mix hardware outputs and capture sources; port-level routing for multi-channel interfaces; effect chains (builtin and LADSPA); devices that survive unplug, replug and sleep; live meters everywhere.

Five frontends on one D-Bus service: Plasma window with tray and global shortcuts, web UI for phones and headless boxes, CLI, Stream Deck plugin, and your own. 102 numbered requirements, 101 proven by automated tests against a private PipeWire.
